block.title: The supplier
block.name: usl_b2c_supply
block.help: Who fulfils print-on-demand orders, what it costs and where it is paid from.

setting.help: A read-only token. Without it a drop cannot ask the supplier what an order cost or when it shipped.
Who draws on the wallet, and who the monthly supply document is billed by.
The journal holding the prepaid balance the supplier draws on. A top-up pays into it and a month of supply empties it.
What the supplier's fulfilment of a sale is bought as, so it reaches the cost-of-sales account.
What a fulfilment answering to no sale is bought as. It is the cost of finding out what to sell, never the cost of something sold.

block.title: Where the money meets the bank
block.name: usl_b2c_transfers
block.help: A channel collects for weeks and pays out once. These say where that payout waits for its statement line.

setting.help: The bank the channels pay into and the wallet is topped up from. Its suspense account is where a payout waits.
Where the entries for payouts and top-ups are written, so they read as one movement rather than as bookkeeping inside a bank.

block.title: What a sale owes
block.name: usl_b2c_vat
block.help: Goods dispatched from another Member State owe destination VAT from the first euro.

setting.string: Registered for the One Stop Shop
setting.help: Until registration, destination VAT accrues as a liability to be regularised rather than as VAT collected under a scheme the shop is not in.

A consumer buying goods and a business buying services are both untaxed for entirely different reasons. Nothing in a customer record tells them apart, so the position for consumer goods is named rather than deduced. Leave it empty to let the fiscal positions decide.
